title: One more cow on the shared field
hook: Ten herders, one pasture. Every choice is sensible. What happens to the grass?

doesNotKnow: how each person's sensible choice can ruin a shared resource
that the gain from using more is private while the cost is shared

misconception: If everyone is rational, the shared resource will be fine.
objective: The learner can explain that when a resource is shared with no rules, each user gains the whole benefit of using more but bears only a share of the cost, so everyone uses more and the group ends up worse off.

claims.text: With 10 cows, each cow earns 20 − 10 = 10, so each herder earns 10 and the group earns 100.
claims.source: Model rule: each cow earns 20 − N. N = 10 → 10 per cow; 10 × 10 = 100.

claims.text: If you alone add a second cow, there are 11 cows each earning 9, so you earn 18 and every other herder earns 9.
Adding a cow gives the adder a whole cow's earnings, while the crowding cost (each cow earns 1 less) is spread across all cows.
claims.source: Model rule: adding one cow lowers every cow's earnings by 1; the adder gains the new cow's 20 − (N + 1) minus 1 per cow they already own.

claims.text: If the other herders each add a cow whenever it raises their own income, after the first round there are 18 cows earning 2 each, and the group earns 36 instead of 100. This happens whether you add a cow or keep.
claims.source: Demo.tsx othersChoose(): a herder with 1 cow adds when 2 × (19 − N) > 20 − N, i.e. N < 18. If you add (N = 11), herders add up to N = 18; if you keep (N = 10), eight herders add, N = 18. 18 × (20 − 18) = 36.

claims.text: Group income n × (20 − n) is highest at 10 cows (100) and falls to 0 at 20 cows.
Real communities often manage shared resources successfully with their own rules.
claims.source: Elinor Ostrom, Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action (Cambridge University Press, 1990).

claims.text: The lesson is a model with made-up numbers: no ownership, no rules, no communication between herders.
claims.source: Assumptions of the lesson's own calculation in Demo.tsx (after Hardin, 'The Tragedy of the Commons', Science 162, 1968).

recall.question: A lake is open to everyone, with no rules. Why does each fisher keep adding boats even as catches fall?
options: Fishers do not notice the fish declining
Each gains a whole extra catch, but the cost of overfishing is shared by all
More boats always means more fish in total
recall.why: The gain from one more boat goes to its owner; the harm (fewer fish for each boat) is spread across everyone, so each sensible choice adds up to overuse.
